A.explanation: Combined regime is the national extremist/propaganda system plus an occupied, militarised city with pervasive checkpoints, arbitrary unofficial detention, torture and acute sexual-violence risk for LGBTQ+ detainees, and no local remedy. Outing can trigger extremism investigation, detention and severe custodial abuse; execution is not documented. This is state-directed targeting well below B, which lacks the local detention/checkpoint layer.

entry_documents.exposure: 2023 ban on gender-affirming surgery and marker changes; no recognition route, so foreign passport mismatch can be checked. Occupied city has pervasive checkpoints and document checks; non-holders treated as stateless.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at checkpoint can lead to investigation, stateless treatment and detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 101 extremism convictions nationally; participation in designated movement up to 12 years in local summary; arbitrary detention in unofficial sites, no lawyer/family access, documented torture and lethal-risk death in custody nationally.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No local protective institution, monitor or remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Checkpoint/document encounter can escalate directly to unofficial detention where abuse including sexual violence is documented as acute risk.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access rule specifically documented; marker ban creates universal mismatch exposure in any sex-segregated setting.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Mismatch plus detention creates birth-sex placement/service risk, but specific placement rule is not documented.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming surgery banned 2023; no marker change. Medication seizure, HRT continuity and emergency ward placement not documented for visitors.
care_services.interaction: Care ban is resident-facing in part, but signals institutional hostility; no visitor care protection documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Supreme court designated non-existent international LGBT movement extremist Nov 2023; propaganda law extended to all ages Dec 2022, 180+ cases in 2023, 18-fold growth, raids on LGBT bars within 48 hours, 100 patrons searched/photographed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Expression, symbols, venues and association are policed as extremism, so discovery can become a criminal case.

minors_guardians.exposure: Propaganda law prohibits material promoting non-traditional relationships and giving minors desire to change sex, extended to all ages. Travelling with a minor increases expression/material exposure; specific guardian-detention rule not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent/guardian expression or care-seeking with a minor can trigger propaganda/extremism scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Masked police raids, searches, arrests; 74% say homosexuality should not be accepted (2022); no anti-discrimination protection, gender/sexual-orientation motive not aggravating, hate crimes not officially recorded.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hostile public attitudes plus police as raiding actor means police are perpetrator, not protector, if outed.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Country left regional human-rights court 2022; no local remedy in occupied city; highest do-not-travel advisory; legal-aid, consular access in unofficial detention not documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of remedy compounds checkpoint-to-detention pathway; absence is not treated as safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Safer than 0.05 because execution for trans presentation is not documented, but A shares state detention, lethal custodial risk and torture; approaching this tier.
More dangerous than 0.15-B: B-like imprisonment and ill-treatment are compounded by militarised checkpoints, unofficial sites, no lawyer/family access and documented acute sexual-violence risk.
Far below 0.35-A, where consequence is exclusion without imprisonment; here extremism convictions, up to 12 years, raids and custodial torture are documented.
Far below 0.85-A, which has enforceable equality protections and functioning oversight; A has opposite state framing and no operating remedy.

A.synthesis: A is not merely the national regime: the occupied city adds universal outing probability via checkpoints and a custodial pathway with torture/sexual violence and no remedy. National extremism/propaganda enforcement supplies the legal lever to arrest; local occupation supplies harsher detention. Interaction, not any single statute, drives the very low score.

B.explanation: National regime alone: no gender recognition, extremist designation of the LGBT movement, 101 extremism convictions, expanding propaganda enforcement, police bar raids, a death in pretrial detention on extremism charges, hostile attitudes and no anti-discrimination/hate-crime aggravation. No division-specific mitigation or additional detention layer is documented. State targeting makes travel severely unsafe, but the occupied-city torture/checkpoint layer in A is absent.

entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch is a climate and scrutiny risk; dossier does not document border officers rejecting foreign documents, so do not overstate entry refusals.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 101 extremism-related convictions by June 2025 under administrative and criminal codes; arrests for rainbow symbols; man on extremism charges over LGBT travel agency found dead in pretrial detention Dec 2024.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Expression/association discovery can lead to extremism charges and pretrial detention where lethal risk is documented in at least one case.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No specific bathroom, ward or custody placement rule documented; marker ban creates mismatch in sex-segregated settings generally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility consequence is extrapolated only from document mismatch, not from a documented facility ban.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State frames LGBT association/expression as extremist, so outing can become investigation and prosecution.

minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a minor widens expression/material exposure for caregiver and child.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection; country left regional human-rights court 2022; highest do-not-travel advisory; division-specific enforcement, court practice and remedies are explicitly unresolved/not documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns are not safety: thin division data resolves toward the documented national targeting pattern.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to 0.15-A: criminalised presentation/extremism, arrests, custodial abuse risk and illusory remedies. B lacks documented routine beatings in custody and capital provision, so slightly above.
Below 0.25-A, where raids/extortion usually end in fines or short detention and execution/imprisonment is rare; B has 101 criminal extremism convictions and a custodial death.
Well below 0.35-A exclusion-only regime; B involves criminal convictions, imprisonment exposure and state raids, not only admission refusal.
Far below 0.85-A enforceable equality and oversight; B has no documented working protection and active extremist enforcement.

B.synthesis: B's operative regime is national state targeting without a documented local sanctuary or harsher local layer. The extremist/propaganda lever, police raids, hostile public attitudes and absence of recourse interact: outing risks investigation, prosecution/detention and no hate-crime protection. It is safer than A only because A's checkpoints and unofficial torture detention are not documented for B.
